hyperedges.label: Five stakeholder feedback forms with per-form scales
Locked decisions enforced in the database, not the UI
Zero-budget architecture stack (SPA, Supabase, RLS, Edge Function, Workers)

nodes.label: Curriculum Feedback & Analysis Platform (PRD)
nodes.rationale: Static forms (Google Forms) gave the college no central user management, no role-based routing and no built-in analysis, so admins could not edit questions, control respondents, or turn responses into insight.

nodes.label: Role-Based Form Routing (FR-7)
nodes.rationale: Each stakeholder type answers a different question set, so the user is sent to the form matching their assigned type instead of choosing one.

nodes.label: Per-Form Likert Rating Scales
nodes.rationale: Scales differ per source form and are preserved as given rather than unified, because rewriting them would misrepresent the college's existing instruments; duplicated rating blocks are treated as copy-paste artifacts and used once.

nodes.label: Question Versioning on Edit (FR-31)
nodes.rationale: Editing text/type/scale/options inserts a new immutable version instead of mutating the row, so past responses stay bound to the exact wording answered and averages plus year-over-year comparisons stay accurate. Cosmetic changes (is_required, order) update in place to avoid version churn.

nodes.label: Question Soft Delete (FR-32)
nodes.rationale: is_active = false removes a question from the live form while its historical answers remain available to analytics and exports; a hard delete would silently destroy past data.

nodes.label: Stable question_key Across Versions
nodes.rationale: Gives every version of a question one grouping key so trends can follow it across rewordings.

nodes.label: One Submission per User per Course per Cycle (FR-15)
nodes.rationale: Keeps data dedupe-free while staying forgiving: a repeat visit upserts on the unique key and opens the existing response for editing rather than inserting a duplicate.
nodes.norm_label: one submission per user per course per cycle (fr-15)

nodes.label: Editable-Until-Cycle-Close Window (FR-16)
nodes.rationale: Writes are allowed only while now() < academic_cycles.closes_at, enforced in an RLS policy rather than the UI so a stale browser tab cannot post after the cycle closes.

nodes.label: Academic-Year Feedback Cycles
nodes.rationale: Organising feedback per academic year matches forms that already ask for the year and enables year-over-year comparison.

nodes.label: CSV Bulk User Import (FR-23)
nodes.rationale: Promoted from optional to required by the 100-500 user scale decision; import previews rows, validates, reports per-row errors and skips duplicates.

nodes.label: Temporary Password on Account Creation (FR-24)
nodes.rationale: Accounts are created directly with a unique temporary password that must be replaced at first sign-in; invite status is deliberately not stored.

nodes.label: Custom Free SMTP Provider for Supabase Auth
nodes.rationale: Supabase's built-in sender is rate-limited to a few messages per hour, far too slow for hundreds of users; a free third-party provider (Brevo/Resend) is wired in as custom SMTP and kept swappable via config so switching providers needs no code change.
nodes.norm_label: custom free smtp provider for supabase auth

nodes.label: Zero-Budget Free-Tier Constraint
nodes.rationale: Every stack and analytics choice is bounded by a zero rupee budget, which is why sentiment is lexicon-based and hosting/DB stay on free tiers.

nodes.label: Row-Level Security Enforcement (NFR-3)
nodes.rationale: Integrity rules (one-per-course, edit window) live in the database/RLS layer, not only client-side, so a direct API call cannot bypass them.

nodes.label: Rule-Based Lexicon Sentiment Analysis (FR-40)
nodes.rationale: True AI sentiment would require a paid API, so v1 uses free lexicon/rule-based scoring; LLM analysis is an explicit stretch goal, not committed.

nodes.label: Auto-Generated Rule-Based Insights (FR-41)
nodes.rationale: Keyword-frequency and ranking rules produce statements like lowest-rated aspect or most requested addition without any model cost.

nodes.label: CSV Export of Raw Responses (FR-42)
nodes.rationale: Export carries question version metadata so historical rewording stays visible in the data.

nodes.label: PDF Summary Report per Academic Year (FR-43)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly nice-to-have and named as one of the first items to defer if Week 3 slips.
nodes.norm_label: pdf summary report per academic year (fr-43)

nodes.label: Version-Aware Analytics and Trend Grouping (FR-34/FR-39)
nodes.rationale: Analytics group by question_key and surface a version count so a mixed average spanning reworded variants is never presented as one consistent question.

nodes.label: Supabase Backend (Postgres, Auth, RLS, Edge Functions)
nodes.norm_label: supabase backend (postgres, auth, rls, edge functions)

nodes.label: Cloudflare Workers Static Assets Hosting
nodes.rationale: Chosen over Vercel because Vercel's Hobby tier refuses deploys authored by anyone but the account owner, blocking a 4-person team; Cloudflare Pages was the original plan but is closed to new projects, so Workers static assets is the supported replacement.

nodes.label: Static Program Lists vs Admin-Managed Course Catalog (A5 / Open Question 1)
nodes.rationale: Course identity for the uniqueness constraint is the entered course_title, so free-text entry with inconsistent spellings weakens the one-per-course rule - the main argument for replacing static dropdowns with a managed catalog.
nodes.norm_label: static program lists vs admin-managed course catalog (a5 / open question 1)

nodes.norm_label: public.profiles table (id, email, full_name, role, status)

nodes.label: supabase/functions/invite-users Edge Function
nodes.rationale: Runs on Supabase rather than locally so account creation works even from npm run dev; it creates confirmed accounts directly and returns a temporary password instead of emailing an invite.

nodes.label: service_role key never reaches the browser
nodes.rationale: The service_role key bypasses every RLS policy, and Vite inlines any VITE_ variable into the shipped bundle, so the key lives only inside the Edge Function where Supabase injects it from its own environment - there is no key to copy anywhere.
nodes.norm_label: service_role key never reaches the browser

nodes.label: Unique index on responses (user_id, cycle_id, course_key)
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.rationale: Makes duplicates impossible at the storage layer; the app upserts on the index so a repeat visit edits the existing row.
nodes.norm_label: unique index on responses (user_id, cycle_id, course_key)

nodes.label: course_key generated column (lowercase, collapsed whitespace)
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.rationale: Normalising the course title makes 'Linear Algebra' and 'linear  algebra' collide rather than both counting, which is the direct answer to the free-text course-identity risk raised in PRD A5.

nodes.label: Edit window checked inside the RLS policy
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.rationale: Writes are permitted only while now() < cycle.closes_at, checked in the policy itself so a stale browser tab or a direct API call cannot post after close.
nodes.norm_label: edit window checked inside the rls policy

nodes.label: Trigger blocking edits to an answered question version
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.rationale: answers reference a question_versions row, never a questions row, and the trigger raises an exception on any attempt to modify a version that already has answers, so history cannot be rewritten even by mistake.
nodes.norm_label: trigger blocking edits to an answered question version

nodes.label: Soft delete (is_active = false) keeps analytics data
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.norm_label: soft delete (is_active = false) keeps analytics data

nodes.label: CSV import in bounded batches with a temporary-password file
nodes.source_location: How the locked decisions are enforced
nodes.norm_label: csv import in bounded batches with a temporary-password file

nodes.label: Scale-aware normalisation (axisFor, bounds from rating_scale_options)
nodes.rationale: Faculty use a 4-point scale while the others use 5-point, so raw averages are not comparable: bounds come from rating_scale_options per scale rather than a literal 5, since assuming 5 would report a 3.5 faculty average as 63% instead of 83% and make faculty look systematically harsher. Non-scoring options such as 'Not applicable' carry a NULL score and are excluded from averages instead of counting as zero, and axisFor() refuses to return a mixed raw axis at all.

nodes.label: Three separate denominators: n_answers, n_scored, and their difference
nodes.rationale: Distributions, averages and non-scoring options each need their own denominator; sharing one is what makes Likert bars appear to sum past 100%.
nodes.norm_label: three separate denominators: n_answers, n_scored, and their difference

nodes.label: analytics_admin_ok() guard in plpgsql functions
nodes.source_location: Analytics reads are admin-only, and fail loudly
nodes.rationale: The analytics functions are SECURITY INVOKER so RLS scopes rows normally, but that alone would show a non-admin aggregates of their own responses with no way to tell, so the guard raises instead. The table-returning functions are plpgsql rather than sql because in a sql body the guard sits inside the row-producing path and the planner skips it once RLS empties that path - handing the non-admin a dashboard of zeros; perform runs before any row work.

nodes.label: Revoke execute from PUBLIC, grant back to authenticated
nodes.source_location: Analytics reads are admin-only, and fail loudly
nodes.rationale: Revoking execute from anon does nothing on its own because create function grants to PUBLIC and anon inherits through it.
nodes.norm_label: revoke execute from public, grant back to authenticated

nodes.label: CSV export excludes identity answers by question_key
nodes.rationale: Dropping user_id does not de-identify an export because name, SAP number and contact details are themselves answers to ordinary form questions; they are excluded by question_key with no opt-in, since a downloaded file has left the app's access controls behind.
nodes.norm_label: csv export excludes identity answers by question_key

nodes.label: papaparse escapeFormulae on free text
nodes.rationale: A quoted cell is still an executable formula when an admin opens the file in Excel.

nodes.label: react-router 7 RSC CSRF advisory trade-off
nodes.rationale: The unfixed high-severity advisory needs React Server Components mode, which a plain Vite SPA with no server runtime cannot enter, and no patched 7.x exists. Downgrading to v6 would trade it for an XSS-via-open-redirect advisory whose pattern this app does use (return-to-where-you-were after login), so v7 is kept and the redirect is hardened in safeRedirect() instead.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Workers deployment (wrangler.jsonc, no main entry)
nodes.rationale: VITE_ variables must be build-time because Vite inlines them into the bundle, so runtime vars are too late. Team members deploy free on Cloudflare, whereas Vercel's Hobby tier fails a second contributor's push.
nodes.norm_label: cloudflare workers deployment (wrangler.jsonc, no main entry)

nodes.label: SPA fallback: not_found_handling returns index.html
nodes.rationale: Cloudflare Pages is closed to new projects so there is no public/_redirects; serving index.html for unmatched paths is what lets a hard refresh on /admin/users reach the router instead of 404ing. No Worker script ever runs - the app is a pure SPA.

nodes.label: Manual first-admin bootstrap SQL
nodes.rationale: Only admins can register users, so the first admin row must be inserted by hand against auth.users.

nodes.label: Temporary password distribution guidance
nodes.rationale: Temporary passwords are shown once, so they must be shared privately and the downloaded credentials file deleted; the database withholds the app role until the password is replaced.

nodes.label: npm run check test suite
nodes.rationale: Covers redirect safety, validation, admin logic, answer remapping across question versions, and the analytics scale/sentiment/insight/CSV rules.
